title: Enumerations, enum constants and underlying integer considerations
learningObjectives: Define an enum with meaningful named constants.
Use enumerators as integer constant expressions.
Understand that enum values are integer values and can be converted.
Avoid assuming a fixed underlying enum representation across implementations.
Validate externally supplied integer values before treating them as a valid enum state.

understand.concept: An enum defines an enumeration type and named integer constant values called enumerators. Enumerators are integer constant expressions. C does not guarantee one universal underlying integer representation for every enum type across implementations, so portable interfaces should not assume a fixed size or binary encoding without an explicit contract.
understand.whyItMatters: Named states are clearer than unexplained numeric codes, but programs should not assume every enum has a fixed width or external representation.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
## 1. Define named states

An enum groups related named values, such as NEW, ACTIVE and CLOSED. This makes state-oriented code easier to read than unexplained numeric constants.

## 2. Enumerator values

Unless explicit values are assigned, enumerators are assigned successive integer values starting at zero. Explicit values can be used when an interface requires particular constants.

## 3. Use enum objects

Declare objects using the enum type and compare them with named enumerators. The compiler can help make the intended state clearer, but C does not enforce that every possible integer value is one of the named enumerators.

## 4. Validate external values

Data read from a file, network or user input may not correspond to a valid enumerator. Check the value against the allowed set before using it as a state.

## 5. Avoid representation assumptions

The compatible integer type is implementation-defined within the standard's constraints. Do not assume enum size or raw representation for portable serialization.

questions.explanation: C enum objects can hold integer values beyond the listed enumerators.
